naslov: The Family's Arrival and the Fulfilment of the Dream

segmenti.tekst: نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنَ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “We relate to you the best of stories in revealing to you this Qur’an, though before it you were among the unaware.” (Yusuf 12:3)

segmenti.tekst: Surah Yusuf: after Yusuf revealed his identity to his brothers and informed them that he was Yusuf, he forgave them for what they had done to him, to his brother, to their father. He ordered them to take his shirt and go to his father in Palestine, to place it on his face, and his sight would return to him.

Since Yaqub, alayhis-salam (peace be upon him), had lost his sight from great pain and weeping – "wabyaddat 'aynahu" – and his eyes, it says, had turned white. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Fa lamma an ja'al-bashiru alqahu 'ala wajhihi fartadda basira."

And after the caravan from Egypt came to Palestine, the bearer of glad tidings, the one who brings joyful news, came to Yaqub, alayhis-salatu was-salam, with the shirt, and, it says, he placed it on Yaqub's face – "fartadda basira".

Everyone around Yaqub was present there, his sons, relatives and so on. And, it says, his sight returned, the sight of Yaqub, alayhis-salatu was-salam, returned. "Fartadda basira. Qala alam aqul lakum inni a'lamu minallahi ma la ta'lamun." He says: "Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know?" Yaqub turned to those present, to his relatives and his sons, and said: "Did I not tell you

that I know from Allah what you do not know?" How? Because Yaqub was a prophet, revelation came to him, so he knew from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, what others did not know. Also, on the basis of the dream that Yusuf had seen and had told only to him, Yaqub knew that everything would end well, but, as a parent, he worried.
What do his sons say to him? When they saw that they had done wrong, they say: "O our father, ask forgiveness for us.
Ask forgiveness for us, truly we have done wrong." We did wrong when we accused you of going too far in that love for Yusuf.
We did wrong in throwing Yusuf into the well. We did wrong in accusing him, his brother, of theft. So pray for us. Pray that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, forgives us, forgives our sins.

So here, dear brothers, as the scholars say, it is permissible for a person to say to his brother: "Make dua (supplication) for your brother, that Allah forgives my sins," and so on. Meaning, from this we can derive this ruling: if a person sees that someone is good, pious and so on, he may say to him: "Make dua for your brother,

make dua for your brother, that Allah forgives my sins," and so on, or for relief in hardship, and so on. Yaqub, alayhis-salam, says to them: "Sawfa astaghfiru lakum Rabbi, innahu huwal-Ghafurur-Rahim."

And Yaqub did not forgive at once, it says. Not only did he forgive them, he says: "I will ask forgiveness for you." And it is mentioned there in the tafsirs that he asked forgiveness for them in the last third of the night, when we pray the night prayer, when Muslims pray the night prayer.

Why? The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), says in a mutawatir hadith – meaning, that is the highest degree of authenticity of a hadith, a mutawatir hadith – narrated by both Bukhari and Muslim, he says: "Yanzilu Rabbuna kulla laylatin ilas-sama'id-dunya."
He says: Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, descends every night to the lowest heaven. How does Allah descend? In the manner that befits Him, subhanahu wa ta'ala.
"Hina yabqa thuluthul-laylil-akhiru" – he says: when the last third of the night begins. "Fa yaqulu: man yad'uni fa astajiba lahu" –

He says: is there anyone who calls upon Me, so that I may answer him? "Wa man yas'aluni fa u'tiyahu" – He says: who asks of Me, is there anyone who asks of Me, so that I may give him? "Wa man yastaghfiruni fa aghfira lahu" – He says: is there anyone who seeks forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?

And that is why the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, prayed the night prayer, that voluntary prayer, in the last third of the night, because at that time the supplications are accepted, the supplications of the believers are accepted. So Yaqub says: "Sawfa astaghfiru lakum Rabbi."

He says: I will ask forgiveness for you, especially in the last third of the night. "Innahu huwal-Ghafurur-Rahim" – truly He is the One who forgives much. Al-Ghafur means the One who forgives much; ar-Rahim, the One who is merciful towards His servants.

After that the whole family, the whole tribe, sets out from Palestine to Egypt. They arrive in Egypt to Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Fa lamma dakhalu 'ala Yusufa awa ilayhi abawayhi" – He says: when they came in to Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, it says, Yusuf embraced his parents, Yusuf embraced Yaqub and his mother. "Wa qaladkhulu Misra in sha Allahu aminin" – he says: enter Egypt,
if Allah wills, in safety – safe from persecution, from hunger, from everything.
وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ
segmenti.prevod: “And he raised his parents upon the throne…” (Yusuf 12:100)

segmenti.tekst: And it says: he raised his parents onto the throne, onto his throne, where he sat, where he resided. And, it says, they made prostration to him, a prostration of greeting.
We have said that in the earlier sacred laws the prostration of greeting – or the prostration of greeting, let us call it that, tahiyyah, meaning prostration of greeting – was prescribed.

Likewise, we also have the example when Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, commanded the angels to prostrate, that is, to prostrate to Adam, and they prostrated. That is the prostration of greeting; it was prescribed in the earlier sacred laws, revelations. With the coming of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and the Qur'an it was abrogated, that ruling was abrogated.

So today it is not permissible for a person to make a prostration of greeting to anyone else. And, it says, they made, they made a prostration of greeting to Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam. He says: "O my father, this is," he says, "the interpretation of the dreams, or the dream, that I saw."

"Ra'aytu ahada 'ashara kawkaban wash-shamsa wal-qamara ra'aytuhum li sajidin." When I saw in a dream eleven stars – and the eleven stars are his eleven brothers – "wash-shamsa" – the sun, his mother – "wal-qamara" – and the moon, his father. He says: "ra'aytuhum li sajidin" – he says: I saw them prostrating to me. He says: so this is, he says, the interpretation, he says, of that dream, that dream I saw

when I was seven years old. Allah has now made it come true. And he says: Allah, he says, has dealt kindly with me when He brought me out of prison. See, dear brothers, he did not mention being thrown into the well.

Why? Because he had completely forgiven his brothers. He did not want to put them in a difficult position, to reproach them. And that is why a person, when he forgives his Muslim brother, should not reproach him for it at every step: "Well, I forgave you, I did this for you, I did that for you." Rather, when a person forgives, he should forgive, and not mention what happened between the two of them.

He further says: "وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِي إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِي مِنَ السِّجْنِ وَجَاءَ بِكُمْ مِنَ الْبَدْوِ" – and he says: my Lord has dealt well and kindly with me, after He, he says, brought you from the desert.

He did not want to say "from poverty, from want", but rather, he says, "from the desert". How fine he was in his words, so as not to hurt them! "Min ba'di an nazaghash-shaytanu bayni wa bayna ikhwati" – after, he says, Shaytan had sown discord between my brothers and me.

He did not want, it is said, to offend them by saying: "My brothers did wrong, they threw me into the well"; rather, he attributed a little of the blame to himself too, so that they would be on the same level.

"Inna Rabbi latifun lima yasha'" – truly, he says, Allah, he says, is subtle in what He wills. "Innahu, innahu huwal-'Alimul-Hakim" – truly He is the One who knows everything and who is the Wise, who knows why, why all this happened. And that wisdom of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, came out, it became visible after everything ended well, after everything ended well, after all of it ended. Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam… here the story of Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, ends.

He says: "Rabbi qad ataytani minal-mulki" – he says: my Lord, he says, You have granted me, he says, authority – "wa 'allamtani min ta'wilil-ahadith" – he says: and You have taught me the interpretation of dreams. "Fatiras-samawati wal-ardi, anta waliyyi fid-dunya wal-akhirah" – Creator of the heavens and the Earth, You are my protector in this world and in the world to come. "Tawaffani musliman" – he says: take my soul as a Muslim – "wa alhiqni bis-salihin" – and join me with the righteous:

the prophets, the martyrs (shuhada), the good servants of Allah – and what wonderful company, the company in Jannah (Paradise). Dear brothers, when Yusuf here supplicates "tawaffani musliman" – he says: take my soul as a Muslim – Yusuf here is not calling for death, he does not wish for death to come to him; rather, he supplicates, he asks Allah to take his soul as a Muslim. And there is no greater privilege for a person than that Allah takes his soul and grants him a good ending.

You know well, the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says that towards the end of this dunya (this world) a time will come when a person will start his day as a believer and wake up as an unbeliever.
It is not so in the literal sense; rather, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, is informing us of the speed with which a person turns away, or, let's say, abandons the religion.

And there are many such examples, that a person – you see him, he prays, everything is nice, great – the next day, let me say the next day, but after some time he is nowhere to be seen in the mosque, nor… rather, you might see the person in a tavern, and so on.

Meaning, he has given it up, he has become an apostate (murtad). That is why a person should, as I mentioned the other night, in the night prayer, recite this supplication: "Ya muqallibal-qulub" – O You who turn the hearts – "thabbit qalbi 'ala dinik" – make my heart firm upon Your religion; "Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana" – our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided them.

So these should be standard supplications, our supplications: that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, makes us firm in this religion and, of course, takes our souls upon it, in sha Allah. Here we have finished Surah Yusuf. Tomorrow… there is still a little left of Surah Yusuf, a part of the surah that is addressed to our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.
So, in sha Allah, tomorrow we will finish that last part as well. In sha Allah. May Allah grant you every good, and we will see each other tomorrow.
